keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Kuninda row. The infobox area is "the southern areas of modern Himanchal, Uttarakhand and western Nepal" with no boundaries; the Dehradun and Shimla radii are the researcher's reading. The page names the Sutlej, Yamuna, Beas and Ganges as rivers of the region (Ptolemy, undated) and Kalsi in Garhwal. Cliopatria draws this land as Shunga (-170 to -67, 38 cells), Indo-Greek (132 cells at -100), Kanva (133 at -50) and Kushan (170 cells, 100-237), so the Kuninda state would be a vassal or republic inside those shapes, which the page does not say.

ledger.note: c. 150 BCE: the Kuninda state is documented. The page says the kingdom is "documented from around the 2nd century BCE to the 3rd century CE" and the infobox gives "Before 2nd century BCE-3rd century"; the first coinage dates "around the 1st century BCE". -150 is the middle of the 2nd century BCE, a bridge. No ruler or event is dated; Amoghabhuti, the best-attested ruler, is placed "late 2nd century-1st century BCE".

ledger.note: c. 250: the Kuninda kingdom disappears. "The Kuninda kingdom disappeared around the 3rd century" (page); 250 is the middle of the 3rd century, a bridge. The page names neither a successor nor a cause, and says nothing of the Kushans, the Yaudheyas (only coin hoards) or the Guptas.

certainty.note: No border is given; the extent is a region named by modern provinces and rivers.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks. One page opened (budget 2-5), and it is thin: the page carries a banner "needs additional citations", names no capital, no wars, no overlord and no events, so both ends are confidence 1 bridges. The Kunindas (Panini: an Ayudhajivi Sangha, a warrior republic) may be a republic rather than a kingdom; the dossier follows the page title. Cliopatria draws the same foothills as Shunga, Indo-Greek, Kanva and Kushan territory, so a gap-filler should open a page that says whether the Kunindas were tributaries (the Yaudheya dossier of sa-02-d starts 200 on the Kushan lands). Gazetteer names needed: Kalsi, Garhwal (text only).
